question: What is the default join type of pandas merge according to the data wrangling handbook, and how many rows does the data_orders dataset contain?
answer: The default join type of pandas merge is an inner join [S3]. The data_orders dataset contains 30 rows [S2].

citations.title: Data Wrangling Handbook
citations.text:
3. Combining Tables
pd.merge joins two DataFrames on key columns. The default is an inner join, which keeps only
keys present in both tables. A left join keeps every row of the left table and fills unmatched
right-hand columns with NaN.
If a key is duplicated in both tables the result contains every pairing of the matching rows, so the
row count can grow (a many-to-many join). pd.concat stacks tables; by default it stacks vertically
(axis=0).

S1.title: Data Glossary
S1.text:
NULL: the SQL marker for a missing value.
NaN: floating-point not-a-number used by pandas for missing numeric data.
None: Python's null object; pandas also treats None as missing in object columns.
key: the column or columns used to match rows when joining two tables.
schema: the names and data types of the columns of a table.
sample: DataFrame.sample(n=3) returns 3 random rows. It is a row draw, not a statistical sample design.
merge versus join: pd.merge joins on columns by default, whereas DataFrame.join joins on the index by default.
index: depends on context - database index, pandas Index or list position.
